short.EN: Ask an AI agent about your rig in plain English: it reads your equipment, logs and frames, and asks before it touches anything

long.EN:
WHAT IT IS FOR
You are imaging and something is off - guiding went bad an hour ago, the focus drifted, a frame came back empty. Instead of digging through tabs and log files yourself, you ask in plain English and the agent looks: it reads your equipment state, the night's log and the frames you saved, and tells you what it finds. If the fix needs an action - restart guiding, plate solve and recentre, stop the sequence - it asks you first. Every time.

WHAT YOU NEED
The agent itself is opencode (https://opencode.ai): a free, open-source AI agent that you install separately, plus a model for it to use - a paid API key, or one running locally on your own machine. Your choice. This plugin contains no AI and installs none, so your models, your keys and your MCP servers stay yours and keep working exactly as they do in your terminal. If opencode is not installed, the panel says so and does nothing else.

WHAT IT GIVES YOU
- The agent in a dock panel: ask a question or hand it a job while you are imaging, without leaving NINA and without a terminal.
- Every permission request in front of you. It asks before it runs a command, edits a file or uses a tool, and this panel is where you answer. Nothing runs unseen. Interrupt at any time.
- NINA itself as tools: camera, mount, focuser, filter wheel, guiding, plate solving - 179 of them, through an MCP server the plugin sets up for you.
- Three agents, differing in what they are allowed to do rather than in tone. observer reads and explains and moves nothing - that is what you get by default. copilot acts, but stops and asks first. autopilot is the unattended one: no prompts anywhere, every permission decided in advance, and a short list of actions that can save a night (restart guiding, plate solve and recentre, stop or start the sequence, set tracking, park the mount, close the shutter). It cannot slew, unpark, open a shutter, throw a switch or connect a device.
- An observatory log: equipment state changes, autofocus runs and one line per saved frame, one file per night. It moves nothing and calls no model, and the agent can read it - so a diagnosis starts from what happened, not only from what is happening now.
- Two ways to connect: launch a local opencode server from the executable on this machine, or attach to one already running elsewhere - on the observatory PC, for instance, while you sit at another.

WHY IT IS SEPARATE FROM THE AI ASSISTANT PLUGIN
The AI Assistant plugin is self-contained: its own providers, its own keys, its own tool loop. This one holds none of that on purpose. Use it if you already run opencode, or if you would rather configure one agent once and reach it from everywhere instead of keeping a second AI setup inside NINA.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO YET
Nothing wakes the agent up. The autopilot agent exists and its policy is enforced, but no event triggers it: you choose it by hand. Unattended operation is being built log-first on purpose, so that what the agent reacts to is decided from what your observatory actually does rather than from a plausible list.

Changes: Out of the beta channel. The plugin is now listed for everyone in the plugin manager, instead of only for people who had turned beta plugins on

Said what it is for. The old description assumed you already knew what opencode is, and told everybody else the plugin was not for them. It now opens with the thing it actually does: you are imaging, something looks wrong, and you ask in plain English instead of digging through tabs and log files

Verified against the current opencode (1.19.1) before release: tool names still carry the server prefix, opencode's own default is still to allow what no rule names, and this plugin's rules are still merged last. The deny floor was checked against a live server rather than asserted - an unnamed tool resolves to deny for all three agents
First published release. A dock panel that connects to an opencode server you installed yourself, either by launching one locally or by attaching to one already running on another machine

Every permission policy opens with a deny floor, and all 179 tools of the N.I.N.A. MCP server are named as opencode actually offers them - {server}_{tool}. A tool that matches no rule is refused instead of allowed, so one that is misnamed, renamed or added by a later server arrives denied and the agent says so. A test compares the generated rules against the names the pinned server really registers, and the release does not publish if it is red

The MCP server is fetched at a fixed release tag and the commit that tag points at is verified after checkout; a mismatch means it does not run. Its dependencies are installed from that release's own pinned requirements. Point the options at your own copy and it is used as it is, with the panel saying it is not the verified release

The server password is offered only when scheme, host and port match the server you configured, and attaching refuses an address that is neither on this machine nor https. An attached server runs under somebody else's configuration, so the panel reports whether that workspace carries this plugin's policy at all
Every permission the agent is waiting on appears at the top of the panel with Allow once, Always and Reject - the agent does not run a command, edit a file or use a tool until somebody answers
Interrupt a running turn at any time

A launched server binds to 127.0.0.1 and carries a password only if you set one. Generating one per launch was tried and removed: the embedded browser never answered the challenge, so the panel took a 401 and stayed blank while an invented credential sat in memory where nobody could type it. What keeps the server private is the address it listens on

Three agents rather than two. observer reads and explains, copilot acts and asks first, and autopilot runs unattended: its permissions are all decided in advance with no "ask" anywhere, because with nobody at the keyboard a prompt is not caution, it is a session that stops at three in the morning. It may restart guiding, plate solve and recentre, stop or start the sequence, set tracking, and park the mount and close the shutter - and nothing else. It cannot slew, unpark, open a shutter, throw a switch or connect a device

Observatory log: the plugin records equipment state changes and one line per saved frame into its own folder, one file per night. It moves nothing and calls no model. It is there so that what an unattended agent should react to can be decided from what this observatory actually does, rather than from a plausible list of events
